facts.fact: “如果让 X 和 Y 交配会得到什么”型笑话常是儿童最爱，看似简单，其实一点不简单
facts.anchor: Jokes beginning with ‘What do you get if you cross …’ are often beloved by children, which can give the impression that they’re incredibly straightforward, but they’re anything but.

facts.fact: 羊＋袋鼠＝woolly jumper（毛线套衫／毛茸茸的跳跃者），第一个例子是文字游戏
facts.anchor: a sheep crossed with a kangaroo results in, yes, a woolly jumper

facts.fact: 大象＋袋鼠＝澳大利亚到处是大坑，第二个例子转向超现实而非双关
facts.anchor: an elephant crossed with a kangaroo leads to big holes all over Australia

facts.fact: 椅子＋仙人掌：问答双方都不知道答案，笑点在“我可不把屁股放上去”——用拒绝回答来解构形式
facts.anchor: What do you get if you cross a chair with a cactus? / I don’t know / Nor do I, but I’m not putting my bum anywhere near it.

facts.fact: 带一袋武器过境会得到什么：Detained（被拘留）——把格式拿去做字面/政治笑话
facts.anchor: What do you get if you cross an international border with a bag of weapons? / Detained.

facts.fact: paraprosdokian：一句话的结尾改变前半句意义的单行笑话，只有语言学家会喜欢这个词
facts.anchor: The kind of word only a linguist could love, a paraprosdokian is a one-liner where the end of a sentence transforms the meaning of the beginning of it.

facts.fact: 类似手法叫 pull back and reveal，但可以在更大篇幅上做；paraprosdokian 理想情况下只在一行内完成
facts.anchor: A similar thing is sometimes referred to as a ‘pull back and reveal’, but that can be on a larger scale, while a paraprosdokian does it in, ideally, a line.

facts.fact: 格劳乔·马克思“我度过了一个完美的夜晚，但不是今晚”是教科书例子：结尾否定前半句
facts.anchor: Groucho Marx’s line ‘I’ve had a perfectly wonderful evening, but this wasn’t it’, is a textbook example.

facts.fact: 斯蒂芬·金谈写作方法：I have the heart of a small boy, in a jar on my desk——结尾把温情变成恐怖
facts.anchor: Horror writer Stephen King, when asked about his approach to writing, once said ‘I have the heart of a small boy, in a jar on my desk.’

facts.fact: 套路段子用 stock characters（固定角色）：高贵骑士、智慧老妪、悲伤小丑，从《天方夜谭》到即兴喜剧都有，是让故事快速启动的文化速记
facts.anchor: Stock characters are a long literary and dramatic convention

facts.fact: 旅行推销员笑话：推销员在某处过夜、陷入尴尬处境，常涉及农夫的女儿，作者直言多数并不好
facts.anchor: Travelling salesman jokes tend to involve the salesman spending the night somewhere and getting into sticky situations

facts.fact: 小吉米笑话：小男孩极度粗俗/醉酒/好色，或无意中泄露父母的私生活；有时笑点只是意外的污，常配一点文字游戏
facts.anchor: Little Jimmy jokes, meanwhile, are based around the idea of a small boy being as unimaginably sweary/drunk/lascivious/offensive as possible, or unwittingly revealing something about his parents’ private lives.

facts.fact: non-sequitur 拉丁语意为“不成立”，转折不仅意外，而且荒诞、无逻辑
facts.anchor: Latin for ‘does not follow’, a non-sequitur usually involves a joke or story taking a turn which isn’t just unexpected, it is absurd and nonsensical and involves no logic at all.

facts.fact: 九岁左右的孩子热衷编 non-sequitur 笑话：传统开头（多少条鱼能换灯泡）＋完全不回答任何问题的包袱（Hatstand! Spaceship! Wibble wibble!）
facts.anchor: Children around the age of nine often get heavily into making up non-sequitur jokes along the lines of a traditional joke setup
